answer: Hardware-rooted remote attestation curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to cryptographically prove execution within a secure enclave. An adversary incurs the scarce capital cost of procuring physical silicon and ferrous server enclosures per alias, preventing a ripple of counterfeit personas. Peers verify these signatures before granting a jade tier of operational trust. However, this approach depends on centralized chip foundries and excludes virtual agents lacking dedicated hardware.
